evals.name: fetch-if-stale-upgrade
evals.prompt: hey, we bumped @data-client to 0.19 in our issue tracker (it's installed already). can you finish the upgrade so everything works like before? it's a git repo, commit is fine to leave to me.
evals.setup: Copy files/issue-tracker to a temp dir outside any skills root and `git init` + commit it. In node_modules, symlink @data-client/{core,endpoint,react,rest,codemods} to this repo's packages, plus react, @types/react, @types/jest and typescript (.bin/tsc) from the repo's node_modules. Run `yarn build:types` first. No jest runner: the agent can't run tests.
evals.expected_output: Codemod run; issueLoader awaits fetchIfStale and drops the instanceof branch; warmIssue (behind an isPromise() helper the codemod can't see) uses the resolved data; settingsLoader keeps its DEFAULT_SETTINGS fallback via catch, since the awaited call now rejects; the test mock resolves; the owner is told Sentry's global handlers no longer see unawaited failures.
assertions: issueLoader awaits `fetchIfStale(IssueResource.get, …)` and no longer branches on `instanceof Promise`.
warmIssue in prefetch.ts uses the resolved data (await or `.then`) instead of the `isPromise()` check, and a `.then()` chain ends in `.catch()`.
settingsLoader still returns DEFAULT_SETTINGS when the settings fetch fails, via `.catch()` or try/catch around the awaited call.
The `Promise.resolve()` wrapper around the comments prefetch is gone, and no `.catch()` is added to bare unawaited calls such as the IssueLink hover prefetch.
The test's fetchIfStale spy uses `mockResolvedValue` (or otherwise resolves its value).
The final message tells the owner that unawaited fetch failures no longer reach Sentry's global handlers and suggests the error reporting Manager without adding it.

evals.name: managers-upgrade
evals.prompt: hey, we bumped @data-client to 0.19 in our chat app (it's installed already). can you finish the upgrade so everything works like before? commit is fine to leave to me.
evals.setup: Same as eval 1, with files/chat-app, and also symlink @data-client/test and @data-client/normalizr.
evals.expected_output: Codemod run; LiveManager defines middleware, opens its socket in init() and keeps `received` across cleanup(); PresenceManager gets a pass-through middleware; each store gets new Manager instances instead of the codemod's `() => managers` around a shared array; AuditNetworkManager stops reading cleanupDate; the renderDataHook test includes a NetworkManager; the console script uses __DC__.
assertions: LiveManager defines a `middleware` property and no `getMiddleware`.
LiveManager opens the WebSocket in `init()`, not in the constructor or `middleware`, and closes it in `cleanup()`.
LiveManager's `cleanup()` no longer clears `received`, and the send in `middleware` is guarded against a closed or missing socket (e.g. `this.socket?.send`).
Each store gets new Manager instances: `managers` is a function that constructs them, and App does not pass `() => managers` around a module-level array.
The renderDataHook test's `managers` function includes a `NetworkManager`.
scripts/dump-store.js reads `__DC__.controller` (setting `__DC__.store` is optional) instead of `__DC_CONTROLLERS__`.
